title: Rabbi Yose Madaa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Chullin 51a mentions him in Rav Safra’s words to Abaye: “Look at this rabbinic scholar who has come from the West and says, ‘My name is Rav Avira.’” In his account, Rav Huna of Tzippori and Rabbi Yose Madaa sat before Rabbi the Great. Rashi identifies that Rabbi as Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi; Hyman refers to his earlier argument that Rabbi Yochanan is intended.

notes.text: Chullin 51a spells out Rav Huna of Tzippori; ר״ה is not head of the academy here. Rabbi the Great is the seated authority, not Rav Avira. Rashi’s identification as Yehudah HaNasi and Hyman’s Yochanan interpretation remain distinct.

The consulted Chullin 51a names Rav Huna of Tzippori and Rabbi Yose Madaa before Rabbi. Rashi explicitly identifies Rabbi as Yehudah HaNasi; the Yochanan identification remains Hyman’s separate argument.
